passages.text: For the choirmaster. According to Mahalath. A Maskil of David.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
He gave instructions to the choirmaster.
He said to use the tune called Mahalath.
This psalm is a Maskil, which means it is a teaching song.

passages.text: The fool says in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt; their ways are vile. There is no one who does good.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
He wrote it for Mahalath.
He wrote it as a maskil, which is a teaching song.
A fool says in his heart, “There is no God.”
These people are corrupt.
They do evil things.
No one among them does good.
passages.original: לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ עַֽל־ מָחֲלַ֗ת מַשְׂכִּ֥יל לְדָוִֽד׃ אָ֘מַ֤ר נָבָ֣ל בְּ֭לִבּוֹ אֵ֣ין אֱלֹהִ֑ים הִֽ֝שְׁחִ֗יתוּ וְהִֽתְעִ֥יבוּ עָ֝֗וֶל אֵ֣ין עֹֽשֵׂה־ טֽוֹב׃

passages.text: God looks down from heaven upon the sons of men to see if any understand, if any seek God.
passages.sermon:
God is in heaven.
God looks down from heaven.
God sees the sons of men.
God wants to know if anyone understands.
God wants to know if anyone seeks Him.
passages.original: אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֗ים מִשָּׁמַיִם֮ הִשְׁקִ֪יף עַֽל־ בְּנֵ֫י אָדָ֥ם לִ֭רְאוֹת הֲיֵ֣שׁ מַשְׂכִּ֑יל דֹּ֝רֵ֗שׁ אֶת־ אֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: All have turned away, they have together become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one.
passages.sermon:
All people have turned away from God.
They have all become corrupt together.
No one does good.
Not even one person does good.
passages.original: כֻּלּ֥וֹ סָג֮ יַחְדָּ֪ו נֶ֫אֱלָ֥חוּ אֵ֤ין עֹֽשֵׂה־ ט֑וֹב אֵ֝֗ין גַּם־ אֶחָֽד׃

passages.text: Will the workers of iniquity never learn? They devour my people like bread; they refuse to call upon God.
passages.sermon:
The workers of iniquity do evil.
They do not learn.
They eat my people as they eat bread.
They do not call upon God.
passages.original: הֲלֹ֥א יָדְעוּ֮ פֹּ֤עֲלֵ֫י אָ֥וֶן אֹכְלֵ֣י עַ֭מִּי אָ֣כְלוּ לֶ֑חֶם אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים לֹ֣א קָרָֽאוּ׃

passages.text: There they are, overwhelmed with dread, where there was nothing to fear. For God has scattered the bones of those who besieged you. You put them to shame, for God has despised them.
passages.sermon:
God acts with power against those who oppose His people.
God causes fear to fall on them.
They feel dread, even when there is nothing to fear.
God scatters the bones of those who attack you.
You put your enemies to shame.
God has rejected them.
passages.original: שָׁ֤ם׀ פָּֽחֲדוּ־ פַחַד֮ לֹא־ הָ֪יָה֫ פָ֥חַד כִּֽי־ אֱלֹהִ֗ים פִּ֭זַּר עַצְמ֣וֹת חֹנָ֑ךְ הֱ֝בִשֹׁ֗תָה כִּֽי־ אֱלֹהִ֥ים מְאָסָֽם׃

passages.text: Oh, that the salvation of Israel would come from Zion! When God restores His captive people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad!
passages.sermon:
God is the one who saves Israel.
God’s salvation comes from Zion.
God restores His people when they are captives.
Jacob will rejoice when God restores His people.
Israel will be glad when God brings them back.
passages.original: מִ֥י יִתֵּ֣ן מִצִּיּוֹן֮ יְשֻׁע֪וֹת יִשְׂרָ֫אֵ֥ל בְּשׁ֣וּב אֱ֭לֹהִים שְׁב֣וּת עַמּ֑וֹ יָגֵ֥ל יַ֝עֲקֹ֗ב יִשְׂמַ֥ח יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
